newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers quiet, few cargoes in Med.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers quiet, few cargoes in Med.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carriers (VLCCs) held onto their recent gains in quiet trade on Tuesday without showing much sense of direction, brokers said.
"It's steady but not really dynamic," said one broker who had expected a fairly strong market this week after VLCC rates fell as low as W45/50 earlier this month.

Nevertheless, Mideast/Japan VLCCs held up at around W62.5, with the 1995-built Golden Stream said fixed at W65 for GSSK, while the ultra-large, 500,000 tonne Kapetan Giannis was done at W50/52.5 Mideast/USG-Red Sea for Vela.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs were also steady at W65.
Vessels of 130,000 tonnes (Suezmaxes) were little changed at about W95.

In the Mediterranean, Suezmaxes were fixed at W90/95 and 80,000 tonners (Aframaxes) at W100/102.5 in quiet trade with few cargoes seeking ships. "But some owners may be willing to settle for less on a private basis," one broker said.
The inter-U.K./Cont Aframax market was also dull, with rates unchanged around W90.
Fuel oil looked slightly livelier than other European sectors, with one broker expecting enquiry to increase over the next few days as Baltic exports become available.
But rates were little changed for now, with inter-U.K./Cont 25,000 tonne stems at W190 and cross-Med at W180.
In the Western hemisphere, 70,000 tonne crude cargoes firmed to W180/185 from W172.5 in date-driven business, while 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems were steady at W215.
